- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 2–3 day lagged mean reversion filter to smooth out over-optimistic peaks.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in early periods; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for first 7–10 days of forecast horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or negative), model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast flat; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to avoid flat forecasts unless sentiment is truly neutral.
